requests.prompt: Children's picture-book illustration in the style of Arnold Lobel's 1971 book The Ice-Cream Cone Coot and Other Rare Birds: fine brown-black pen-and-ink line with delicate crosshatching and stippling, soft transparent watercolour washes in a slightly faded early-1970s print palette (lemon and mustard yellow, olive and sage green, dusty pink and mauve, strawberry pink, ochre, slate blue, warm grey), on cream paper with visible grain. Whimsical, gentle and slightly eerie, dreamlike mood. No text, no lettering, no watermark, no border, no UI. Exactly the same bird as in its delivered portrait (same design, proportions, colours, line and texture; use that portrait image as the reference), at the same scale, facing left, with only the change described.  The Broomwhisk (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hoai2k/mini/main/icecreamcone/game/assets/subjects/broomwhisk.png): an old straw broom alive as a bird; the long ochre broomstick is its neck, with a small head on top, a pinkish crest, one round pale-yellow eye and a long slate-blue beak pointing left; its body is the bound straw head of the broom (a bulb of straw tied with twine bands), whose loose ochre-and-pink straw bristles hang like a skirt above two thin ochre legs with dark claws. Two poses side by side on one sheet, each in its own half, at the same scale, facing left, standing on its legs: left, mid-sweep, the broomstick neck leaning back to the right and the straw skirt dragged back to the right, its tips brushing the floor; right, flicking, the straw skirt fanned out and swept hard forward to the left along the floor with a few bits of straw flying. Feet at the bottom of each cell. PAINTED AGAIN, at one scale: the delivered sheet painted the head at the portrait's size but the broom about 12% smaller (its binding 0.80 to 0.93 of the portrait's), so no single size fits the whole bird. Paint the Broomwhisk in every cell at exactly the scale of its portrait painting: the head (from the beak's tip to the back of the eye) and the broom (the width of the twine binding, the length of the broomstick neck) all the same size as in the portrait, in every pose. Same poses as before. Transparent background (PNG with alpha). If transparency is not possible, use a flat pure magenta #FF00FF background with nothing else on it and no cast shadow; it is keyed out on integration.
